title.zh: 卷一百 志第五十三 禮三
title.raw: 卷一百 志第五十三 禮三 Volume 100 Treatises 53: Rites 3

sentences.zh: 北郊祈穀五方帝感生帝

translations.literal: Northern Suburb; Praying for Grain; Five-Direction Emperors; Life-Generating Emperor
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb; Praying for Grain; the Five-Direction Emperors; the Life-Generating Emperor

sentences.zh: 北郊。

translations.literal: The Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 宋初，方丘在宮城之北十四里，以夏至祭皇地祇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, the square mound altar was fourteen li north of the palace city, and at the summer solstice they sacrificed to Imperial Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song, the square mound altar stood fourteen li north of the palace city; at the summer solstice the court sacrificed to Imperial Earth there.

sentences.zh: 別為壇於北郊，以孟冬祭神州地祇。

translations.literal: A separate altar was established at the northern suburb, and in the first month of winter they sacrificed to the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.
translations.idiomatic: Another altar was set up at the northern suburb, where in mid-winter they sacrificed to the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.

sentences.zh: 建隆以來，迭奉四祖崇配二壇。

translations.literal: Since Jianlong, they successively honored four ancestors with elevated status as correlates at the two altars.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jianlong era onward, four ancestors had in turn been elevated as correlates at the two altars.

sentences.zh: 太平興國以後，但以宣祖、太祖更配。

translations.literal: After Taiping Xingguo, only Emperor Xuanzu and Emperor Taizu were alternately made correlates.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiping Xingguo, only Xuānzǔ and Tàizǔ served alternately as correlates.

sentences.zh: 真宗乃乙太宗配方丘，宣祖配神州地祇。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong then moved Emperor Taizong to be correlate at the square mound altar and Emperor Xuanzu as correlate for the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong then assigned Taizong as correlate at the square mound altar and Xuānzǔ as correlate for the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，禮官言：「皇地祇壇四角再成，面廣四丈九尺，東西四丈六尺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, the ritual officials said: "The altar to Imperial Earth has four corners and two tiers; its face is four zhang nine chi wide, and east to west it is four zhang six chi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangyou, ritual officials reported: "The altar to Imperial Earth has four corners and two tiers; its face measures four zhang nine chi across, and four zhang six chi from east to west.

sentences.zh: 上成高四尺五寸，下成高五尺，方五丈三尺，陛廣三尺五寸，卑陋不應典禮。

translations.literal: The upper tier is four chi five cun high, the lower tier five chi high, square and five zhang three chi, with steps three chi five cun wide—low and shabby, not fitting canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The upper tier stands four chi five cun high, the lower five chi; the platform is five zhang three chi square, with steps only three chi five cun wide—too mean for canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 請如唐制增廣之。」

translations.literal: We ask that it be enlarged according to Tang regulations."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that it be enlarged to match Tang practice."

sentences.zh: 五年，諸壇皆改。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, all the altars were altered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, all the altars were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐配位七十一，加羊、豕各五。

translations.literal: In Jiayou there were seventy-one correlate positions, with five sheep and five pigs added for each.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiayou there were seventy-one correlate positions, with five sheep and five pigs added to the offerings.

sentences.zh: 慶曆用犢、羊、豕各一。

translations.literal: In Qingli they used one calf, one sheep, and one pig each.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingli the offerings were one calf, one sheep, and one pig each.

sentences.zh: 既而諫官司馬光奏：「大行請諡於南郊，而皇地祇止於望告，失尊卑之序。」

translations.literal: Later Remonstrance Bureau official Sima Guang memorialized: "The late emperor's posthumous title was requested at the southern suburb, yet Imperial Earth received only a prospect sacrifice—this reverses the order of honor and subordination."
translations.idiomatic: Later the remonstrator Sima Guang submitted: "The late emperor's posthumous title was sought at the southern suburb, while Imperial Earth received only a prospect sacrifice—this inverts the proper order of honor."

sentences.zh: 下禮院，定非次祭告皇地祇，請差官詣北郊行事。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Ritual Academy, which fixed an extraordinary sacrifice to announce it to Imperial Earth and asked that an official be dispatched to the northern suburb to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Ritual Academy, which scheduled an extraordinary announcement to Imperial Earth and requested an official be sent to the northern suburb to conduct the rite.

sentences.zh: 其神州之壇，方三丈一尺，皇祐增高三尺，廣四十八步，內壝四面以青繩代之。

translations.literal: The altar for the Divine Land was square, three zhang one chi; in Huangyou its height was increased by three chi and its breadth to forty-eight paces; on four sides of the inner enclosure green cord was used in place of a wall.
translations.idiomatic: The altar for the Divine Land was a square three zhang one chi across; in Huangyou its height was raised three chi and its breadth set at forty-eight paces, with green cord marking the inner enclosure on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 仍遣內臣降香，有司攝事如儀。

translations.literal: They still sent a palace eunuch to deliver incense, and the relevant offices performed the rite by proxy according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch was still sent to deliver incense, while the relevant offices conducted the rite by proxy as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐元年二月，郊廟奉祀禮文所言：「古者祀天於地上之圜丘，在國之南，祭地於澤中之方丘，在國之北，其牲幣禮樂亦皆不同，所以順陰陽、因高下而事之以其類也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, the suburban and temple sacrifice ritual text stated: "In antiquity Heaven was sacrificed to at the Circular Mound on the ground, south of the state; Earth was sacrificed to at the Square Mound in the marsh, north of the state. Their victims, silks, ritual, and music were all different, thereby following yin and yang and, according to high and low, serving each with its proper kind.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanfeng 1, the suburban and temple sacrifice ritual text stated: "In antiquity Heaven was sacrificed to at the Circular Mound on open ground south of the state, and Earth at the Square Mound in the marsh north of the state. Victims, silks, ritual, and music all differed, following yin and yang and serving each deity according to its proper kind.

sentences.zh: 由漢以來，乃有夫婦共牢，合祭天地之說，殆非所謂求神以類之意。

translations.literal: From Han onward there arose the doctrine of husband and wife sharing one pen and jointly sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—hardly the meaning of seeking spirits by kind.
translations.idiomatic: From Han onward came the doctrine of husband and wife sharing one pen and jointly sacrificing to Heaven and Earth—hardly the meaning of seeking spirits by kind.

sentences.zh: 本朝親祀上帝，即設皇地祇位，稽之典禮，有所未合。」

translations.literal: Our dynasty, when personally sacrificing to August Heaven, also sets a place for Imperial Earth—examined against canonical ritual, this is not fully proper."
translations.idiomatic: When our dynasty personally sacrificed to August Heaven, it also set a place for Imperial Earth—examined against canonical ritual, this was not fully proper."

sentences.zh: 遂詔詳定更改以聞。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered detailed revision and amendment to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered detailed revision and amendment to be reported.

sentences.zh: 於是陳襄、王存、李清臣、張璪、黃履、陸佃、何洵直、楊完等議，或以當郊之歲，冬夏至日分祭南北郊，各一日而祀遍；

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Xiang, Wang Cun, Li Qingchen, Zhang Suo, Huang Lü, Lu Tian, He Xunzhi, Yang Wan, and others deliberated: some proposed that in years of suburban sacrifice, the winter and summer solstice days should separately sacrifice at the southern and northern suburbs, each completed in one day;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiang, Wang Cun, Li Qingchen, Zhang Suo, Huang Lü, Lu Tian, He Xunzhi, Yang Wan, and others then deliberated: some proposed that in suburban-sacrifice years, the winter and summer solstices should separately sacrifice at the southern and northern suburbs, each on its own day;

sentences.zh: 或於圜丘之旁，別營方丘而望祭；

translations.literal: some proposed building a separate Square Mound beside the Circular Mound and performing a prospect sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: some proposed building a separate Square Mound beside the Circular Mound and performing a prospect sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 或以夏至盛暑，天子不可親祭，改用十月；

translations.literal: some held that at the summer solstice, in intense heat, the Son of Heaven could not sacrifice in person and proposed using the tenth month instead;
translations.idiomatic: some held that midsummer heat made personal sacrifice impossible and proposed using the tenth month instead;

sentences.zh: 或欲親郊圜丘之歲，夏至日遣上公攝事于方丘，議久未決。

translations.literal: some wished that in years of personal suburban sacrifice at the Circular Mound, on the summer solstice day a senior duke be sent to perform the rite by proxy at the Square Mound. Deliberation long remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: some wished that in years of personal Circular Mound sacrifice, a senior duke officiate by proxy at the Square Mound on the summer solstice. Deliberation long remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 三年，翰林學士張璪言：「先王順陰陽之義，以冬至祀天，夏至祀地，此萬世不可易之理。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hanlin Academician Zhang Suo said: "The former kings followed the principle of yin and yang, sacrificing to Heaven at the winter solstice and to Earth at the summer solstice—this is a principle that cannot be altered for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Hanlin Academician Zhang Suo argued: "Former kings honored yin and yang by sacrificing to Heaven at the winter solstice and to Earth at the summer solstice—a principle that must never be changed.

sentences.zh: 議者乃欲改用他月，無所據依。

translations.literal: Those debating the issue wished to use other months, but there is no basis for that.
translations.idiomatic: Proponents of change wanted other months, yet nothing in precedent supports that.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，宜即郊祀之歲，於夏至之日，盛禮容，具樂舞，遣塚宰攝事。

translations.literal: If it absolutely cannot be avoided, then in the year of suburban sacrifice, on the day of the summer solstice, with full ritual display and complete music and dance, send the chief minister to perform the rite by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: If no alternative remains, then in a suburban-sacrifice year, on the summer solstice, with full ceremonial display, music, and dance, let the chief minister officiate by proxy.

sentences.zh: 雖未能皆當於禮，庶幾先王之遺意猶存焉。」

translations.literal: Although it may not all accord with ritual, perhaps the former kings' intent can still be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Even if not every detail matches ritual, something of the former kings' intent might yet be preserved."

sentences.zh: 於是禮官請如璪議，設宮架樂、文武二舞，改制樂章，用竹冊匏爵，增配帝犢及捧俎分獻官，廣壇壝齋宮，修儀注上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ritual officials asked to follow Suo's proposal: set up palace-frame music and civil and military dances, revise the hymn texts, use bamboo tablets and gourd goblets, add a correlate imperial calf and officials to hold the trays and divide the offerings, enlarge the altar, enclosure, and fasting palace, revise the ritual regulations, and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual offices then adopted Suo's plan: palace-frame music and civil and military dances, revised hymns, bamboo tablets and gourd goblets, an added imperial calf as correlate and officers to present the offerings, enlarged altar, enclosure, and fasting palace, with revised regulations submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既而曾肇言：「今冬至若罷合祭，則夏至又以有司攝事，則不復有親祭地祇之時，于父天母地之義若有隆殺。

translations.literal: Later Zeng Zhao said: "If the combined sacrifice is now abolished at the winter solstice, and at the summer solstice the relevant offices again perform by proxy, then there will no longer be a time when the emperor personally sacrifices to Earth—toward Father Heaven and Mother Earth this seems to show elevation and diminution.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zeng Zhao warned: "If combined sacrifice is ended at the winter solstice and summer solstice rites are again left to officials, the emperor will never personally sacrifice to Earth—the honor shown Father Heaven and Mother Earth will be uneven.

sentences.zh: 請遇親祀南郊之歲，以夏至日備禮躬款北郊，以存事地之義。」

translations.literal: We ask that in years when the emperor personally sacrifices at the southern suburb, on the summer solstice day he prepare the full rites and in person attend the northern suburb, to preserve the meaning of serving Earth."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that in years of personal southern-suburb sacrifice, on the summer solstice the emperor perform the full rites in person at the northern suburb, preserving the duty owed to Earth."

sentences.zh: 四年四月，乃詔：「親祀北郊，並依南郊之儀，有故不行，即以上公攝事。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, an edict was issued: "Personal sacrifice at the northern suburb shall follow the southern suburb rites in all respects; if there is cause not to proceed, then a senior duke shall perform by proxy."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year an edict declared: "Personal sacrifice at the northern suburb shall follow southern-suburb practice; if circumstances prevent it, a senior duke shall officiate."

sentences.zh: 六年，禮部、太常寺上親祀儀並如南郊；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted personal-sacrifice regulations identical to the southern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices submitted personal-sacrifice regulations matching the southern suburb;

sentences.zh: 其攝事唯改舞名及不備官，其籩豆、樂架、玉幣之數，盡如親祠。

translations.literal: for proxy performance only the dance names were changed and some offices were not fully staffed; the numbers of offering vessels, music frames, and jade and silk were all as for personal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: proxy rites differed only in dance names and incomplete staffing; counts of offering vessels, music frames, and jade and silk matched personal sacrifice exactly.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月甲辰冬至，祀昊天上帝，以太祖配，始罷合祭，不設皇地祇位。

translations.literal: That year, on the winter solstice day jiachen in the eleventh month, they sacrificed to August Heaven, with Emperor Taizu as correlate, and for the first time abolished the combined sacrifice, not setting a place for Imperial Earth.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice, eleventh month, day jiachen, they sacrificed to August Heaven with Taizu as correlate, ending combined sacrifice for the first time and omitting a place for Imperial Earth.

sentences.zh: 哲宗初立，未遑親祀，有司攝事如元豐儀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong first ascended, he had not yet undertaken personal sacrifice; the relevant offices performed by proxy according to the Yuanfeng regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong first took the throne he had not yet sacrificed in person; officials conducted the rites by proxy under Yuanfeng practice.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年夏至，祭皇地祇，命尚書右丞許將攝事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou, at the summer solstice, they sacrificed to Imperial Earth and ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Jiang to perform by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice in Yuanyou 5 they sacrificed to Imperial Earth, with Vice Director Xu Jiang officiating by proxy.

sentences.zh: 將言：「王者父天母地，三歲冬至，天子親祠，遍享宗廟，祀天圜丘，而夏至方澤之祭，乃止遣上公，則皇地祇遂永不在親祠之典，此大闕禮也。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "The king takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother. Every three years at the winter solstice the Son of Heaven sacrifices in person, offering throughout the ancestral temples and sacrificing to Heaven at the round mound—yet for the square marsh sacrifice at the summer solstice they only send a senior duke, so Imperial Earth is forever excluded from personal sacrifice. This is a great breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang argued: "A king has Heaven for father and Earth for mother. Every three years at the winter solstice the Son of Heaven sacrifices in person, feasting the ancestral temples and Heaven at the round mound—yet at the summer solstice square-marsh rite only a senior duke is sent, so Imperial Earth is permanently shut out of personal sacrifice. This is a grave lapse in ritual.

sentences.zh: 望博詔儒臣，講求典故，明正祀典，為萬世法。」

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will broadly summon Confucian scholars to investigate precedents, clarify and rectify the sacrificial canon, and make it a model for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: He urged a broad summons of scholars to examine precedents, rectify the sacrificial canon, and set a standard for all time."

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書趙彥若請依元豐所定，郊祀之歲，親祀方丘及攝事，已合禮之正，更不須聚議。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zhao Yanruo asked to follow what Yuanfeng had fixed: in years of suburban sacrifice, personal sacrifice at the square mound and proxy performance—this already accords with ritual propriety and needs no further assembly for debate.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zhao Yanruo urged adherence to Yuanfeng: in suburban-sacrifice years, personal square-mound sacrifice with proxy backup already matched proper ritual and needed no further debate.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中崔公度請用陳薦議，仍合祭天地，從祀百神。

translations.literal: Section Director Cui Gongdu asked to adopt Chen Jian's proposal, still combining sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with the hundred spirits as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Section Director Cui Gongdu favored Chen Jian's plan to continue combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with the hundred spirits in attendance.

sentences.zh: 復詔尚書、侍郎、兩省及侍從、台諫、禮官集議。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered Directors, Vice Directors, both provincial secretariats, attendants, censorate remonstrators, and ritual officials to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered directors, vice directors, both secretariats, attendants, censors, and ritual officers to deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 於是翰林學士顧臨等八人，請合祭如故事，俟將來親祠北郊，則合祭可罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hanlin Academician Gu Lin and seven others asked for combined sacrifice as in precedent, until in the future the emperor personally sacrifices at the northern suburb—then combined sacrifice may be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Gu Lin and seven colleagues asked to keep combined sacrifice as before until the emperor could personally sacrifice at the northern suburb, after which it might be ended.

sentences.zh: 宋興，一祖六宗，皆合祭天地，其不合祭者，惟元豐六年一郊爾。

translations.literal: Since the rise of the Song, one ancestor and six emperors all combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; those who did not combine did so only at the one suburban sacrifice of the sixth year of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song rose, one founder and six emperors had all combined Heaven and Earth; only the sixth year of Yuanfeng had seen a single suburban rite without combination.

sentences.zh: 去所易而就所難，虛地祇之大祭，失今不定，後必悔之。

translations.literal: To abandon what is easy and pursue what is difficult, to leave empty the great sacrifice to Earth, to fail to decide now—later there will surely be regret.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the easy course for the hard, to hollow out Earth's great sacrifice, and to leave the question unsettled now would surely invite regret later.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎范純禮等二十二人，皆主北郊之議。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Fan Chunli and twenty-one others all upheld the northern-suburb proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Fan Chunli and twenty-one others all favored the northern-suburb plan.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人孔武仲又請以孟冬純陰之月，詣北郊親祠，如神州地祇之祭。

translations.literal: Drafting Office Attendant Kong Wuzhong further asked that in the first month of winter, the pure yin month, the emperor go in person to the northern suburb to sacrifice, as with the sacrifice to the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Attendant Kong Wuzhong further proposed that in mid-winter, the month of pure yin, the emperor sacrifice in person at the northern suburb, as for the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land.

sentences.zh: 彭汝礪、曾肇復上疏論合祭之非。

translations.literal: Peng Ruli and Zeng Zhao again submitted memorials arguing against combined sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ruli and Zeng Zhao again memorialized against combined sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The texts are mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of their texts are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 九月，三省上顧臨等議。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Three Departments submitted Gu Lin and others' deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Three Departments reported Gu Lin's group's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后曰：「宜依仁宗皇帝故事。」

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said: "We should follow Emperor Renzong's precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said: "Follow Emperor Renzong's precedent."

sentences.zh: 呂大防言：「諸儒獻議，欲南郊不設皇地祇位，於祖宗之制未睹其可。」

translations.literal: Lü Dagfang said: "The scholars' proposal to set no place for Imperial Earth at the southern suburb—I do not see how that accords with our ancestors' institutions."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Dagfang objected: "Scholars want no place for Imperial Earth at the southern suburb—I see no precedent among our ancestors for that."

sentences.zh: 範百祿以「圜丘無祭地之禮，《記》曰：'有其廢之，莫可舉也。

translations.literal: Fan Bailu cited that "the round mound has no rite of sacrificing to Earth; the Record says: 'What has been abolished cannot be revived.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bailu cited that "the round mound has no Earth sacrifice; the Record says, 'What has been abolished cannot be revived.

sentences.zh: '先帝所廢，稽古據經，未可輕改。」

translations.literal: What the late emperor abolished, grounded in antiquity and canonical texts, cannot lightly be changed.'"
translations.idiomatic: What the late emperor ended, grounded in antiquity and canon, must not be lightly reversed.'"

sentences.zh: 大防又言：「先帝因禮文所建議，遂令諸儒定北郊祀地之禮，然未經親行。

translations.literal: Dagfang added: "The late emperor, on the Ritual Text Office's recommendation, had the scholars fix the northern-suburb sacrifice to Earth, yet he never performed it in person.
translations.idiomatic: Dagfang added: "On the Ritual Text Office's advice the late emperor had scholars fix northern-suburb Earth sacrifice, yet he never performed it himself.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝臨禦之始，當親見天地，而獨不設地祇位，恐亦未安。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the emperor's rule he should personally behold Heaven and Earth, yet to set no place for Earth alone—this too may be unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign the emperor should behold Heaven and Earth in person; to omit Earth's place alone may also be unsettling.

sentences.zh: 況祖宗以恩霈四方，慶賚將士，非三歲一行，則國力有限。

translations.literal: Moreover, our ancestors bestowed grace on the four quarters and rewarded officers and soldiers; if it is not once every three years, state resources are limited.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our ancestors showered grace on the realm and rewarded troops; without a three-year cycle, state resources cannot bear the cost.

sentences.zh: 今日宜為勉行權制，俟北郊議定及太廟享禮，行之未晚。」

translations.literal: Today we should strive to enact an expedient measure; wait until the northern-suburb debate is settled and ancestral-temple feasting is arranged—it will not be too late to act."
translations.idiomatic: For now an expedient should suffice; once northern-suburb policy and ancestral-temple feasting are settled, reform will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 太皇太后以大防之言為是。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager deemed Dagfang's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager agreed with Dagfang.

sentences.zh: 而蘇頌、鄭雍皆以「古者人君嗣位之初，必郊見天地。

translations.literal: Su Song and Zheng Yong both cited that "in antiquity when a ruler first succeeded, he had to sacrifice at the suburbs and behold Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Su Song and Zheng Yong both noted that "in antiquity a new ruler had to sacrifice at the suburbs and behold Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝初郊而不祀地，恐未合古。」

translations.literal: Now the emperor's first suburban sacrifice does not include Earth—this may not accord with antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's first suburban rite to omit Earth may not match antiquity."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「國家郊廟特祀，祖宗以來命官攝事，惟三歲一親郊，則先享清廟，冬至合祭天地於圜丘。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "Our state's suburban and temple special sacrifices—since our ancestors, officials have performed by appointment; only once every three years does the emperor sacrifice in person at the suburbs, first feasting the Pure Temple, then at the winter solstice combining sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the round mound.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "For suburban and temple rites our ancestors usually appointed proxies; only every three years does the emperor sacrifice in person—first at the Pure Temple, then at the winter solstice combining Heaven and Earth at the round mound.

sentences.zh: 元豐間，有司援周制，以合祭不應古義，先帝乃詔定親祀北郊之儀，未之及行。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, the relevant offices cited Zhou regulations, holding that combined sacrifice did not accord with ancient meaning; the late emperor then ordered the fixing of regulations for personal sacrifice at the northern suburb, but did not carry them out in time.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng officials cited Zhou practice, arguing combined sacrifice violated antiquity; the late emperor ordered northern-suburb personal sacrifice fixed, but never carried it out.

sentences.zh: 是歲，郊祀不設皇地祇位，而宗廟之享率如權制。

translations.literal: That year suburban sacrifice set no place for Imperial Earth, while ancestral-temple feasting largely followed the expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: That year suburban sacrifice omitted Imperial Earth, while ancestral-temple feasting largely followed expedient practice.

sentences.zh: 朕方修郊見天地之始，其冬至日南郊，宜依熙寧十年故事，設皇地祇位以嚴並況之儀。

translations.literal: We are just beginning to restore suburban beholding of Heaven and Earth; for the winter-solstice southern suburb, we should follow the tenth-year of Xining precedent and set a place for Imperial Earth to enforce the solemn rite of joint presentation.
translations.idiomatic: As I begin restoring suburban communion with Heaven and Earth, this winter solstice at the southern suburb should follow Xining 10 and include Imperial Earth to preserve the solemn joint rite.

sentences.zh: 厥後躬行方澤之祀，則修元豐六年五月之制。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when personally performing the square-marsh sacrifice, we shall follow the regulations of the fifth month of the sixth year of Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When I later perform the square-marsh sacrifice in person, I shall follow the sixth year of Yuanfeng, fifth month.

sentences.zh: 俟郊禮畢，集官詳議典禮以聞。」

translations.literal: After the suburban rites are complete, assemble officials to deliberate the canonical rituals in detail and report."
translations.idiomatic: After suburban rites conclude, officials shall deliberate canonical ritual in detail and report."

sentences.zh: 十一月冬至，親祠南郊，遂合祭天地，而詔罷飲福宴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month at the winter solstice he personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, then combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, and an edict abolished the blessing-feast banquet.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice he sacrificed in person at the southern suburb, combining Heaven and Earth, and abolished the blessing-feast banquet by edict.

sentences.zh: 八年，禮部尚書蘇軾復陳合祭六議，令禮官集議以聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Minister of Rites Su Shi again submitted six arguments on combined sacrifice and ordered ritual officials to assemble for deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Minister Su Shi again submitted six arguments on combined sacrifice and ordered ritual officers to deliberate and report.

sentences.zh: 已而下詔依元祐七年故事，合祭天地於南郊，仍罷集議。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict followed the seventh-year of Yuanyou precedent, combining Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb, and the assembly for debate was still abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict followed Yuanyou 7, combining Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb, and ended further debate.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，以右正言張商英言：「先帝制詳定禮文所，謂合祭非古，據經而正之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, on Right Remonstrator Zhang Shangying's statement: "The late emperor established the Detailed Ritual Text Office, which held that combined sacrifice was not ancient and corrected it according to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 1, Right Remonstrator Zhang Shangying argued: "The late emperor's Detailed Ritual Text Office held combined sacrifice uncanonical and corrected it by the classics.

sentences.zh: 元祐之臣，乃復行合祭，請再下禮官議。」

translations.literal: The Yuanyou ministers have now restored combined sacrifice; we ask that ritual officials deliberate again."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou ministers have restored combined sacrifice; ritual officers should deliberate again."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞黃履謂：「南郊合祭，因王莽諂事元後，遂躋地位，同席共牢。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Huang Lü said: "Combined sacrifice at the southern suburb arose because Wang Mang flattered Empress Yuan, elevating her status to share the same mat and joint victim.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Huang Lü said: "Southern-suburb combined sacrifice began when Wang Mang flattered Empress Yuan, elevating her to share mat and victim with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 迨先帝親郊，大臣以宣仁同政，復用莽意合祀，瀆亂典禮。」

translations.literal: When the late emperor sacrificed in person at the suburbs, grand ministers, because Empress Xuanren shared power, again used Mang's idea of combined sacrifice, profaning and disordering canonical ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor sacrificed in person, ministers citing Empress Xuanren's co-rule revived Mang's combined sacrifice and profaned canonical ritual."

sentences.zh: 帝以詢輔臣，章惇曰：「北郊止可謂之社。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked his chief ministers; Zhang Dun said: "The northern suburb can only be called the community altar."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers; Zhang Dun said: "The northern suburb can only be called the community altar."

sentences.zh: 黃履曰：「郊者，交於神明之義，所以天地皆稱郊。

translations.literal: Huang Lü said: "Suburban sacrifice means communion with the spirits; therefore both Heaven and Earth are called suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Lü replied: "Suburban sacrifice means communion with the spirits; that is why both Heaven and Earth are called suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 社者，土之神爾，豈有祭大祇亦可謂之壯乎？」

translations.literal: The community altar is merely the spirit of soil—how can sacrificing to the Great Spirit also be called suburban sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: The community altar is merely the spirit of soil—how can sacrifice to the Great Spirit also be called a suburban rite?"

sentences.zh: 乃以履奏送禮部、太常寺。

translations.literal: Lü's memorial was then sent to the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lü's memorial was forwarded to the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎盛陶、太常丞王誼等言：「宜用先帝北郊儀注，以時躬行，罷合祭禮。」

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Rites Sheng Tao, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Aide Wang Yi, and others said: "The late emperor's northern-suburb ritual regulations should be used and performed in person at the proper season, abolishing combined sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Acting Vice Minister Sheng Tao, Sacrifices Aide Wang Yi, and others said: "The late emperor's northern-suburb ritual regulations should be used and performed in person at the proper season, abolishing combined sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 已而三省言：「合祭既非禮典，但盛夏祭地祇，必難親行。」

translations.literal: Later the Three Departments said: "Combined sacrifice is already not canonical ritual, but sacrificing to Earth in midsummer would be hard to perform in person."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments added: "Combined sacrifice is uncanonical, yet midsummer Earth sacrifice would be difficult to perform in person."

sentences.zh: 詔令兩省、台諫、禮官同議，可親祀北郊，然後罷合祭之禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered both secretariats, censorate remonstrators, and ritual officials to deliberate together: once personal sacrifice at the northern suburb is possible, then abolish combined sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered both secretariats, censors, and ritual officers to agree: end combined sacrifice only after personal northern-suburb sacrifice is feasible.

sentences.zh: 曾布、錢勰、範純禮、韓宗師、王古、井亮采、常安民、李琮、虞策、劉定、傅楫、黃裳、豐稷、葉祖洽等言，互有是否。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu, Qian Wei, Fan Chunli, Han Zongshi, Wang Gu, Jing Liangcai, Chang Anmin, Li Cong, Yu Ce, Liu Ding, Fu Ji, Huang Shang, Feng Ji, Ye Zuqia, and others spoke, with mutual agreement and disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu, Qian Wei, Fan Chunli, Han Zongshi, Wang Gu, Jing Liangcai, Chang Anmin, Li Cong, Yu Ce, Liu Ding, Fu Ji, Huang Shang, Feng Ji, Ye Zuqia, and others divided for and against.

sentences.zh: 蔡京、林希、蔡六、黃履、吳安持、晁端彥、翟思、郭知章、劉拯、黃慶基、董敦逸等請罷合祭。

translations.literal: Cai Jing, Lin Xi, Cai Liu, Huang Lü, Wu Anchi, Chao Duanyan, Zhai Si, Guo Zhizhang, Liu Zheng, Huang Qingji, Dong Dunyi, and others asked to abolish combined sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, Lin Xi, Cai Liu, Huang Lü, Wu Anchi, Chao Duanyan, Zhai Si, Guo Zhizhang, Liu Zheng, Huang Qingji, Dong Dunyi, and others urged abolishing combined sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed them.

sentences.zh: 然北郊親祀，終帝之世未克舉雲。

translations.literal: Yet personal sacrifice at the northern suburb was never accomplished throughout that emperor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yet personal northern-suburb sacrifice was never achieved in that emperor's lifetime.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，命禮部、太常寺詳定北郊儀制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to fix the northern-suburb ritual system in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong Jingguo 1 the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to finalize northern-suburb ritual.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史彭汝霖又請改合祭之禮，韓忠彥以為不可。

translations.literal: Palace Remonstrance Bureau Attendant Peng Rulin again asked to change combined sacrifice; Han Zhongyan held it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Peng Rulin again sought to change combined sacrifice; Han Zhongyan opposed it.

sentences.zh: 曾布力主北郊之說，帝亦然之，遂罷合祭。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu strongly upheld the northern-suburb proposal; the emperor agreed, and combined sacrifice was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu strongly favored the northern-suburb plan; the emperor agreed, and combined sacrifice ended.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，詔禮制局議方壇制度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe, the Ritual Regulations Bureau was ordered to deliberate the square-altar system.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 3 the Ritual Regulations Bureau was ordered to deliberate the square-altar system.

sentences.zh: 是歲，新壇成。

translations.literal: That year the new altar was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the new altar was completed.

sentences.zh: 初，元豐三年七月，詔改北郊圜壇為方丘。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the seventh month of the third year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered the northern-suburb round altar changed to a square mound.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the third year of Yuanfeng, seventh month, an edict ordered the northern-suburb round altar changed to a square mound.

sentences.zh: 六年，命禮部、太常定北郊壇制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to fix the northern-suburb altar system.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were ordered to fix the northern-suburb altar system.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖三年，權尚書侍郎黃裳等言：「南郊青城至壇所五百一十八步，自瑞聖園至皇地祇壇之東壇五百五十六步，相去不遠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng under Emperor Zhezong, Acting Vice Director Huang Shang and others said: "From the southern-suburb Green City to the altar site is five hundred eighteen paces; from Ruisheng Garden to the eastern altar of the Imperial Earth altar is five hundred fifty-six paces—not far apart.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhezong's Shaosheng 3, Acting Vice Director Huang Shang and others noted: "From the southern-suburb Green City to the altar is 518 paces; from Ruisheng Garden to the eastern Imperial Earth altar is 556 paces—not far apart.

sentences.zh: 其壇系國初所建，神靈顧享已久。

translations.literal: That altar was built at the founding of the state; the spirits have long looked upon it with favor.
translations.idiomatic: That altar dates to the dynasty's founding; the spirits have long received offerings there.

sentences.zh: 元豐間，有司請地祇、神州並為方壇，壇之外為坎，詔止改圜壇為方。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, the relevant offices asked that Earth Spirit and Divine Land both have square altars with pits outside the altars; the edict ordered only that the round altar be changed to square.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng officials proposed square altars for Earth Spirit and Divine Land with pits outside; the edict ordered only conversion of the round altar to square.

sentences.zh: 請下有司，比類南郊增飾制度，除治四面，稍令低下，以應澤中之制。」

translations.literal: We ask that the relevant offices be ordered, following the southern-suburb model to enhance the regulations, clear and work the four sides, and make it slightly lower, to accord with the regulations for the marsh within the fen."
translations.idiomatic: They asked subordinate offices, following southern-suburb precedent, to enhance the design, clear all four sides, and lower it slightly to match marsh-altar regulations."

sentences.zh: 詔禮部再為詳定，指畫興築。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites was again ordered to fix details in full and direct construction.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites was again ordered to finalize details and direct construction.

sentences.zh: 至是，禮制局言：「方壇舊制三成，第一成高三尺，第二成、第三成皆高二尺五寸，上廣八丈，下廣十有六丈。

translations.literal: At this point the Ritual Regulations Bureau said: "The old square-altar system had three tiers; the first tier was three chi high, the second and third tiers each two chi five cun high; the top was eight zhang wide, the base sixteen zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Ritual Regulations Bureau reported: "The old square altar had three tiers—the first three chi high, the second and third each two chi five cun; the top eight zhang wide, the base sixteen.

sentences.zh: 夫圜壇既則象於乾，則方壇當效法於坤。

translations.literal: Since the round altar already takes Qian as its model, the square altar ought to follow Kun as its model.
translations.idiomatic: If the round altar models Qian, the square altar should model Kun.

sentences.zh: 今議方壇定為再成，一成廣三十六丈，再成廣二十四丈，每成崇十有八尺，積三十六尺，其廣與崇皆得六六之數，以坤用六故也。

translations.literal: It is now proposed that the square altar be fixed at two tiers: the first tier thirty-six zhang wide, the second twenty-four zhang; each tier eighteen chi high, totaling thirty-six chi; both breadth and height attain the number six-six, because Kun employs six.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed two tiers: the first 36 zhang wide, the second 24; each 18 chi high, 36 chi total—breadth and height both yielding six-six, since Kun uses six.

sentences.zh: 為四陛，陛為級一百四十有四，所謂坤之策百四十有四者也。

translations.literal: There are four stairways; the steps number one hundred forty-four—the so-called Kun tally of one hundred forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Four stairways with 144 steps—the Kun tally of 144.

sentences.zh: 為再壝，壝二十有四步，取坤之策二十有四也。

translations.literal: There are two enclosures; each enclosure twenty-four paces—the Kun tally of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Two enclosures of 24 paces each—again Kun's tally of 24.

sentences.zh: 成與壝俱再，則兩地之義也。」

translations.literal: Both tiers and enclosures are doubled—this is the meaning of the two earths."
translations.idiomatic: Doubled tiers and enclosures express the duality of Earth."

sentences.zh: 齋宮大內門曰廣禋，東偏門曰東秩，西偏門曰西平，正東門曰含光，正西門曰咸亨，正北門曰至順，南內大殿門曰厚德，東曰左景華，西曰右景華，正殿曰厚德，便殿曰受福、曰坤珍、曰道光，亭曰承休，後又增四角樓為定式。

translations.literal: The fasting palace's great inner gate was called Broad Sacrifice; the east side gate East Order, the west side gate West Peace, the main east gate Containing Light, the main west gate All-Pervading, the main north gate Utmost Compliance, the south inner great-hall gate Thick Virtue; east was called Left Splendid Bloom, west Right Splendid Bloom; the main hall Thick Virtue; side halls Received Blessings, Kun Treasure, and Way's Radiance; the pavilion Received Rest; later corner towers were added as the fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting palace gates were named Broad Sacrifice (main inner), East Order and West Peace (side gates), Containing Light (east), All-Pervading (west), Utmost Compliance (north), and Thick Virtue (south inner hall); east and west wings were Left and Right Splendid Bloom; the main hall Thick Virtue; side halls Received Blessings, Kun Treasure, and Way's Radiance; the pavilion Received Rest; corner towers were later added as standard.

sentences.zh: 其神位，崇甯初，禮部員外郎陳暘言：「五行於四時，有帝以為之主，必有神以為之佐。

translations.literal: As for the spirit positions, at the beginning of Chongning, Ministry of Rites Section Director Chen Yang said: "For the Five Phases through the four seasons, there is an emperor as lord and necessarily a spirit as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: On spirit placements, early in Chongning Section Director Chen Yang argued: "For the Five Phases through the four seasons, each has an emperor as lord and a spirit as assistant.

sentences.zh: 今五行之帝既從享于南郊第一成，則五行之神亦當列於北郊第一成。

translations.literal: Now that the Five-Phase emperors already attend sacrifice at the first tier of the southern suburb, the Five-Phase spirits should also be arrayed at the first tier of the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five-Phase emperors already attend at the southern suburb's first tier, the Five-Phase spirits should be arrayed at the northern suburb's first tier as well.

sentences.zh: 天莫尊於上帝，而五帝次之；

translations.literal: Nothing in Heaven is more honored than August Heaven, and the Five Emperors come next;
translations.idiomatic: In Heaven nothing ranks above August Heaven; the Five Emperors come next;

sentences.zh: 地莫尊於大祇，而嶽帝次之，今尚與四鎮、海瀆並列，請升之于第一成。」

translations.literal: Nothing on Earth is more honored than the Great Spirit, and the mountain emperors come next; they are still arrayed alongside the four guardian mountains and sea and river spirits—we ask that they be elevated to the first tier."
translations.idiomatic: On Earth nothing ranks above the Great Spirit; the mountain emperors come next, yet they still stand with the four guardian mountains and sea and river spirits—we ask that they be raised to the first tier."

sentences.zh: 至是，議禮局上《新儀》：皇地祇位於壇上北方南向，席以稿秸；

translations.literal: At this point the Ritual Deliberation Bureau submitted the New Regulations: Imperial Earth was placed on the altar in the north facing south, with straw-mat seating;
translations.idiomatic: Then the Ritual Deliberation Bureau submitted the New Regulations: Imperial Earth on the altar's north side, facing south, seated on straw mats;

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝位於壇上東方西向，席以蒲越。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu was placed on the altar in the east facing west, with rush-mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu on the east side of the altar, facing west, on rush mats.

sentences.zh: 木神勾芒、東嶽於壇第一龕，東鎮、海瀆於第二龕，東山林、川澤於壇下，東丘陵、墳衍、原隰於內壝之內，皆在卯階之北，以南為上。

translations.literal: Wood Spirit Goumang and the Eastern Peak in the altar's first niche, the Eastern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second niche, eastern mountains, forests, streams, and marshes below the altar, eastern hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all north of the mao steps, with south as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Wood Spirit Goumang and the Eastern Peak in the first niche; the Eastern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; eastern mountains, forests, and waters below the altar; eastern hills, mounds, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all north of the mao steps, ranked toward the south.

sentences.zh: 神州地祇、火神祝融、南嶽於壇第一龕，南鎮、海瀆於第二龕，南山林、川澤於壇下，南丘陵、墳衍、原隰於內壝之內，皆在午階之東，以西為上。

translations.literal: Earth Spirit of the Divine Land, Fire Spirit Zhurong, and the Southern Peak in the first niche; the Southern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; southern mountains, forests, streams, and marshes below the altar; southern hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all east of the wu steps, with west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Earth Spirit of the Divine Land, Fire Spirit Zhurong, and the Southern Peak in the first niche; the Southern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; southern mountains, forests, and waters below; southern hills and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all east of the wu steps, ranked toward the west.

sentences.zh: 土神後土、中嶽於壇第一龕，中鎮於第二龕，中山林、川澤於壇下，中丘陵、墳衍、原隰於內壝之內，皆在午階之西，以西為上。

translations.literal: Earth Spirit Houtu and the Central Peak in the first niche; the Central Guardian Mountain in the second; central mountains, forests, streams, and marshes below the altar; central hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all west of the wu steps, with west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Earth Spirit Houtu and the Central Peak in the first niche; the Central Guardian Mountain in the second; central mountains, forests, and waters below; central hills and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all west of the wu steps, ranked toward the west.

sentences.zh: 金神蓐收、西嶽於壇第一龕，西鎮、海瀆於第二龕，昆侖西山林、川澤於壇下，西丘陵、墳衍、原隰於內壝之內，皆在酉階之南，以北為上。

translations.literal: Metal Spirit Rushou and the Western Peak in the first niche; the Western Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; Kunlun and western mountains, forests, streams, and marshes below the altar; western hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all south of the you steps, with north as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Metal Spirit Rushou and the Western Peak in the first niche; the Western Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; Kunlun and western mountains, forests, and waters below; western hills and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all south of the you steps, ranked toward the north.

sentences.zh: 水神玄冥、北嶽於壇第一龕，北鎮、海瀆於第二龕，北山林、川澤於壇下，北丘陵、墳衍、原隰於內壝之內，皆在子階之西，以東為上。

translations.literal: Water Spirit Xuanming and the Northern Peak in the first niche; the Northern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; northern mountains, forests, streams, and marshes below the altar; northern hills, mounds, plains, and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all west of the zi steps, with east as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Water Spirit Xuanming and the Northern Peak in the first niche; the Northern Guardian Mountain and sea and river spirits in the second; northern mountains, forests, and waters below; northern hills and lowlands within the inner enclosure—all west of the zi steps, ranked toward the east.

sentences.zh: 神州地祇席以稿秸，余以莞席，皆內向。

translations.literal: The Earth Spirit of the Divine Land used straw-mat seating; the rest used rush mats; all faced inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth Spirit of the Divine Land sat on straw mats; the others on rush mats, all facing inward.

sentences.zh: 其餘並如元豐儀壇壝之制。

translations.literal: The rest followed the Yuanfeng regulations for altar and enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed Yuanfeng altar and enclosure regulations.

sentences.zh: 其位板之制，上帝位板長三尺，取參天之數；

translations.literal: As for the position-board regulations: August Heaven's board was three chi long, taking the number of reaching Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Position boards: August Heaven's was three chi long—the number of reaching Heaven;

sentences.zh: 厚九寸，取幹元用九之數；

translations.literal: nine cun thick, taking Qian's number of nine;
translations.idiomatic: nine cun thick—Qian's number nine;

sentences.zh: 廣尺二寸，取天之備數；

translations.literal: one chi two cun wide, taking Heaven's complete number;
translations.idiomatic: one chi two cun wide—Heaven's complete number;

sentences.zh: 書徽號以蒼色，取蒼璧之義。

translations.literal: the honorific title written in azure, taking the meaning of the azure bi.
translations.idiomatic: titles inscribed in azure, matching the azure bi.

sentences.zh: 皇地祇位板長二尺，取兩地之數；

translations.literal: Imperial Earth's board was two chi long, taking the number of the two earths;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Earth's board was two chi long—the number of the two earths;

sentences.zh: 厚六寸，取坤元用六之數；

translations.literal: six cun thick, taking Kun's number of six;
translations.idiomatic: six cun thick—Kun's number six;

sentences.zh: 廣一尺，取地之成數；

translations.literal: one chi wide, taking Earth's complete number;
translations.idiomatic: one chi wide—Earth's complete number;

sentences.zh: 書徽號以黃色，取黃琮之義。

translations.literal: the honorific title written in yellow, taking the meaning of the yellow cong.
translations.idiomatic: titles inscribed in yellow, matching the yellow cong.

sentences.zh: 皆以金飾。

translations.literal: All were ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: All were gilt.

sentences.zh: 配位板各如天地之制。

translations.literal: Correlate boards each followed the regulations for Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Correlate boards matched Heaven and Earth's dimensions.

sentences.zh: 又言：「《大禮格》，皇地祇玉用黃琮，神州地祇、五嶽以兩圭有邸。

translations.literal: They also said: "According to the Great Ritual Standards, Imperial Earth used a yellow cong; the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land and the Five Peaks used paired gui with bases.
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "According to the Great Ritual Standards, Imperial Earth used a yellow cong; the Earth Spirit of the Divine Land and the Five Peaks used paired gui with bases.

sentences.zh: 今請二者並施於皇地祇，求神以黃琮，薦獻以兩圭有邸。

translations.literal: We now ask that both be applied to Imperial Earth: seeking the spirit with the yellow cong, presenting offerings with the paired gui with bases.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that both apply to Imperial Earth: the yellow cong to seek the spirit, paired gui with bases for presentation.

sentences.zh: 神州惟用圭邸，餘不用。

translations.literal: The Divine Land used only the gui base; the rest did not.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Land used only the gui base; the others did not.

sentences.zh: 玉琮之制，當用坤數，宜廣六寸，為八方而不剡；

translations.literal: The jade cong's form should use Kun's numbers: six cun wide, eight-sided and uncut;
translations.idiomatic: The jade cong should follow Kun's numbers: six cun wide, eight-sided and uncarved;

sentences.zh: 兩圭之長宜共五寸，並宿一邸，色與琮同。

translations.literal: the two gui together five cun long, housed in one base, the color the same as the cong.
translations.idiomatic: the paired gui five cun long together, housed in one base, matching the cong's color.

sentences.zh: 牲幣如之。」

translations.literal: Victims and silks followed likewise."
translations.idiomatic: Victims and silks followed the same rule."

sentences.zh: 又言：「常祭，地祗、配位各用冰鑒一；

translations.literal: They also said: "At regular sacrifice, Earth Spirit and correlates each used one ice mirror;
translations.idiomatic: They also noted: "At regular sacrifice Earth Spirit and correlates each had one ice mirror;

sentences.zh: 今親祀，盛暑，請增正配及從祀位冰鑒四十一。」

translations.literal: for this personal sacrifice in great heat, we ask to add forty-one ice mirrors for principal, correlate, and attendant spirits."
translations.idiomatic: for this personal midsummer sacrifice, they asked for forty-one ice mirrors at principal, correlate, and attendant positions."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 四年五月夏至，親祭地于方澤，以皇弟燕王俁為亞獻，趙王亻思為終獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year at the summer solstice, the emperor personally sacrificed to Earth at the square marsh, with his younger brother Prince Yan You as secondary offering and Prince Zhao [Si] as final offering.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice in the fifth month of the fourth year the emperor sacrificed to Earth in person at the square marsh, with his brother Prince Yan You as secondary offering and Prince Zhao [Si] as final offering.

sentences.zh: 皇帝散齋七日於別殿，致齋七日於內殿，一日于齋宮。

translations.literal: The emperor observed dispersed fasting for seven days in a separate hall, full fasting for seven days in the inner hall, and one day in the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fasted in seclusion seven days in a side hall, seven days in the inner palace, and one day in the fasting palace.

sentences.zh: 前一日告配太祖室，其有司陳設及皇帝行事，並如郊祀之儀。

translations.literal: The day before, he announced the correlate at Taizu's chamber; the relevant offices' arrangements and the emperor's actions all followed suburban-sacrifice regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The day before he announced Taizu as correlate; officials' arrangements and the emperor's actions followed suburban-sacrifice practice.

sentences.zh: 是後七年，至宣和二年、五年，親祀者凡四。

translations.literal: Seven years thereafter, down to the second and fifth years of Xuanhe, there were four personal sacrifices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next seven years, through Xuanhe 2 and 5, he sacrificed in person four times in all.

sentences.zh: 高宗紹興初，惟用酒脯鹿ＭＺ，行一獻禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozong's Shaoxing era, they used only wine, dried meats, and venison, performing a one-presentation rite.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozong's Shaoxing reign they offered only wine, dried meats, and venison in a single-presentation rite.

sentences.zh: 二年，太常少卿程瑀言：「皇地祇，當一依祀天儀式。」

translations.literal: In the second year, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cheng Yu said: "Imperial Earth should wholly follow the regulations for sacrificing to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Vice Director Cheng Yu argued: "Imperial Earth should follow Heaven-sacrifice regulations entirely."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「國朝祀皇地祇，設位於壇之北方南向。

translations.literal: He also said: "Our dynasty sacrifices to Imperial Earth with the position on the altar's north side facing south.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "Our dynasty places Imperial Earth on the altar's north side, facing south.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，設于南方北向。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe it was placed on the south side facing north.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 4 it was placed on the south side, facing north.

sentences.zh: 今北面望祭，北向為難，且於經典無據。

translations.literal: Now to sacrifice facing north from the north is awkward, and it has no basis in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing northward from the north is awkward and lacks canonical support.

sentences.zh: 請仍南向。」

translations.literal: We ask that it again face south."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that it face south again."

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，朱熹為先朝南北郊之辯曰：「《禮》'郊特牲而社稷太牢'，《書》'用牲于郊，牛二'及'社於新邑'，此明驗也。

translations.literal: During Chunxi, Zhu Xi argued on the former court's northern and southern suburbs: "The Rites: 'suburban special victim but the altars of soil and grain receive the great victim'; the Documents: 'use victims at the suburb, two oxen' and 'the community altar at the new city'—these are clear proofs.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunxi, Zhu Xi debated the former court's northern and southern suburbs: "The Rites say 'a special victim at the suburb but the great victim at the altars of soil and grain'; the Documents say 'victims at the suburb, two oxen' and 'the community altar at the new city'—clear proof.

sentences.zh: 本朝初分南北郊，後復合而為一。

translations.literal: Our dynasty at first divided the northern and southern suburbs, then later combined them into one.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty first separated northern and southern suburbs, then later merged them.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》亦只說祀昊天上帝，不說祀後土，故先儒言無北郊，祭社即是祭地。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou also speak only of sacrificing to August Heaven, not of sacrificing to Queen Earth; therefore former scholars said there is no northern suburb—sacrificing at the community altar is sacrificing to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou mention only August Heaven, not Queen Earth; former scholars therefore held there is no northern suburb—community-altar sacrifice is Earth sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 古者天地未必合祭，日月、山川、百神亦無一時合祭共用之禮。

translations.literal: In antiquity Heaven and Earth were not necessarily combined in sacrifice; sun, moon, mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits likewise had no rite of combined sacrifice at one time with shared offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Heaven and Earth were not necessarily combined; sun, moon, mountains, rivers, and the hundred spirits had no single rite combining them with shared offerings.

sentences.zh: 古之時，禮數簡而儀從省，必是天子躬親行事，豈有祭天卻將上下百神重遝累積並作一祭耶？

translations.literal: In ancient times ritual was simple and ceremonial retinue spare; the Son of Heaven must have acted in person—how could sacrificing to Heaven pile up upper and lower spirits layer upon layer into one sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient ritual was simple and retinues spare; the Son of Heaven acted in person—how could Heaven sacrifice heap upper and lower spirits into one rite?

sentences.zh: 且郊壇陛級兩邊上下，皆是神位，中間恐不可行。

translations.literal: Moreover, on both sides of the suburban altar's steps above and below are all spirit positions—the center surely cannot be traversed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, spirit positions line both sides of the altar steps—the center could hardly be walked.

sentences.zh: 或問：郊祀後稷以配天，宗祀文王以配上帝，帝即是天，天即是帝，卻分祭，何也？

translations.literal: Someone asked: suburban sacrifice pairs Houji with Heaven; temple sacrifice pairs King Wen with August Heaven—Emperor is Heaven and Heaven is Emperor, yet they are separate sacrifices—why?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: suburban sacrifice pairs Houji with Heaven; temple sacrifice pairs King Wen with August Heaven—Emperor is Heaven and Heaven is Emperor, yet the rites differ—why?

sentences.zh: 曰：為壇而祭，故謂之天，祭於屋下而以神祇祭之，故謂之帝。」

translations.literal: He answered: sacrificing on an altar, therefore it is called Heaven; sacrificing under a roof and treating it as a spirit, therefore it is called Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: sacrifice on an altar is called Heaven; sacrifice under a roof, treating the spirit as such, is called Emperor."

sentences.zh: 祈穀、雩祀。

translations.literal: Praying for Grain and Rain-Prayer Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Praying for Grain; Rain-Prayer Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 宋之祀天者凡四：孟春祈谷，孟夏大雩，皆於圜丘或別立壇。

translations.literal: The Song's sacrifices to Heaven number four in all: in the first month of spring, praying for grain; in the first month of summer, the great rain prayer—both at the round mound or at a separately established altar.
translations.idiomatic: Song sacrifice to Heaven falls into four kinds: spring grain-prayer and summer great rain-prayer, both at the round mound or a separate altar.

sentences.zh: 季秋大饗明堂。

translations.literal: In the last month of autumn, the great feast at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In late autumn, the great feast at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 惟冬至之郊，則三歲一舉，合祭天地焉。

translations.literal: Only the winter-solstice suburb, once every three years, combines sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Only the winter-solstice suburban rite, every three years, combines Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，太祖幸西京，以四月有事南郊，躬行大雩之禮。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, Taizu visited the Western Capital; in the fourth month he had business at the southern suburb and personally performed the great rain-prayer rite.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaibao, Taizu visited the Western Capital and in the fourth month personally performed the great rain-prayer rite at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 淳化、至道，太宗亦以正月躬行祈穀之祀，悉如圜丘之禮。

translations.literal: In Chunhua and Zhidao, Taizong also in the first month personally performed the praying-for-grain sacrifice, all according to round-mound regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chunhua and Zhidao, Taizong also performed grain-prayer in person in the first month, following round-mound practice.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，龍圖閣待制陳彭年言：「伏睹畫日，來年正月三日上辛祈穀，至十日始立春。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, Dragon Diagram Hall Attendant Chen Pengnian said: "We have seen the scheduled day: next year on the third day of the first month, the upper xin day for praying for grain, while the Beginning of Spring comes only on the tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3, Dragon Diagram Attendant Chen Pengnian reported: "The schedule sets grain-prayer on the third day of next year's first month, an upper xin day, while Beginning of Spring falls only on the tenth.

sentences.zh: 按《月令》，正月元日注為祈穀，郊祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: According to the Monthly Ordinances, the first day of the first month is noted as praying for grain, suburban sacrifice to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances mark the first day of the first month for grain-prayer and suburban sacrifice to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：'啟蟄而郊，郊而後耕。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'When the insects stir, suburban sacrifice; after suburban sacrifice, then plowing.'
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'When insects stir, suburban sacrifice; after suburban sacrifice, then plowing.'

sentences.zh: '蓋春氣初至，農事方興，郊祀昊天，以祈嘉穀，當在建寅之月，迎春之後。

translations.literal: For spring qi first arrives and farming is just rising; suburban sacrifice to August Heaven to pray for fine grain should be in the month jianyin, after welcoming spring.
translations.idiomatic: Spring qi is just arriving and farming begins; suburban sacrifice to August Heaven for fine grain belongs in the jianyin month, after welcoming spring.

sentences.zh: 自晉泰始二年，始用上辛，不擇立春之先後。

translations.literal: From the second year of Jin Taishi onward, they began using the upper xin day, not choosing whether it came before or after Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin the second year of Taishi they used the upper xin day without regard to Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: 齊永明元年，立春前郊，議欲遷日，王儉曰：'宋景平元年、元嘉六年並立春前郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qi Yongming, suburban sacrifice before Beginning of Spring—debate wished to move the day; Wang Jian said: 'In Song Jingping 1 and Yuanjia 6 both had suburban sacrifice before Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming 1, with suburban sacrifice before Beginning of Spring, some wanted to move the date; Wang Jian cited Song Jingping 1 and Yuanjia 6, both before Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: '遂不遷日。

translations.literal: So the day was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: So the date was not changed.

sentences.zh: 吳操之云：'應在立春前。

translations.literal: Wu Caozhi said: 'It should be before Beginning of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Caozhi said it should fall before Beginning of Spring.

sentences.zh: '然則左氏所記，乃三代彝章；

translations.literal: Thus what Master Zuo recorded is the constant regulation of the Three Dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: What Master Zuo recorded is the Three Dynasties' constant rule;

sentences.zh: 王儉所言，乃後世變禮。

translations.literal: what Wang Jian spoke is a later age's altered ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's view is a later alteration.

sentences.zh: 來年正月十日立春，三日祈穀，斯則襲王儉之末議，違左氏之明文。

translations.literal: Next year Beginning of Spring is the tenth of the first month but praying for grain is the third—this follows Wang Jian's lesser opinion and violates Master Zuo's explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Beginning of Spring falls on the tenth but grain-prayer on the third—this follows Wang Jian's lesser view and violates Master Zuo's explicit text.

sentences.zh: 望以立春後上辛行祈穀禮。」

translations.literal: We hope the upper xin day after Beginning of Spring may be used for the praying-for-grain rite."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grain-prayer be held on the upper xin day after Beginning of Spring."

sentences.zh: 因詔有司詳定諸祠祭祀。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered the relevant offices to fix in detail the sacrifices at the various shrines.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered officials to fix all shrine sacrifices in detail.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「今年四月五日，雩祀上帝，十三日立夏祀赤帝。

translations.literal: The relevant offices said: "This year on the fifth day of the fourth month is rain-prayer sacrifice to August Heaven; on the thirteenth is Beginning of Summer, sacrifice to the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported: "This year rain-prayer to August Heaven falls on the fifth of the fourth month; Red Emperor sacrifice on the thirteenth, Beginning of Summer.

sentences.zh: 按《月令》：'立夏之日，天子迎夏于南郊。

translations.literal: According to the Monthly Ordinances: 'On the day of Beginning of Summer, the Son of Heaven welcomes summer at the southern suburb.'
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say: 'On Beginning of Summer the Son of Heaven welcomes summer at the southern suburb.'

sentences.zh: '《注》云：'為祀赤帝於南郊。

translations.literal: ' The commentary says: 'to sacrifice to the Red Emperor at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains this as sacrifice to the Red Emperor at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: '又云：'是月也，大雩。

translations.literal: It also says: in this month, the great rain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: in this month, the great rain prayer.

sentences.zh: '《注》云：'《春秋傳》曰：龍見而雩。

translations.literal: ' The commentary says: 'The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: when the dragon appears, rain prayer.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary cites the Spring and Autumn Commentary: when the dragon appears, rain prayer.

sentences.zh: '龍星謂角、亢也，立夏後，昏見於東方。

translations.literal: The dragon star means Horn and Neck; after Beginning of Summer it appears at dusk in the east.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon star is Horn and Neck; after Beginning of Summer it appears at dusk in the east.

sentences.zh: 按《五禮精義》云：'自周以來，歲星差度，今之龍見或在五月，以祈甘雨，于時已晚，但四月上旬卜日。

translations.literal: According to the Essential Meaning of the Five Rites: 'Since Zhou times the annual star has shifted in degree; today's dragon appearance may be in the fifth month—to pray for sweet rain by then is already late, but only the first ten days of the fourth month are used for choosing the day.'
translations.idiomatic: The Essential Meaning of the Five Rites notes: 'Since Zhou the annual star has drifted; the dragon may appear in the fifth month now—too late for sweet rain—so only the first ten days of the fourth month are used to choose a date.'

sentences.zh: '今則惟用改朔，不待得節，祭于立夏之前，殊違舊禮之意。

translations.literal: Today they use only the calendar reform, not waiting for the proper season, sacrificing before Beginning of Summer—this greatly violates the intent of the old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Today they rely only on calendar reform, not waiting for the season, sacrificing before Beginning of Summer—far from old ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 苟或龍見於仲夏，雩祀于季春，相去遼闊，于禮未周。

translations.literal: If the dragon appears in midsummer but rain prayer is in late spring, the distance is vast and the ritual incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: If the dragon appears in midsummer but rain prayer falls in late spring, the gap is too wide for proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 欲請並于立夏後卜日，如立夏在三月，則待改朔。」

translations.literal: We ask that both choose their days after Beginning of Summer; if Beginning of Summer falls in the third month, then wait for the calendar reform."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that both rites choose dates after Beginning of Summer; if Beginning of Summer falls in the third month, wait for the calendar reform."

sentences.zh: 天禧元年十二月，禮儀院言：「准畫日，來年正月十七日祈穀，前二日奏告太祖室，緣歲以正月十五日朝拜玉清昭應宮，景德四年以前，祈穀止用上辛，其後用立春後辛日，蓋當時未有朝拜宮觀禮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianxi, the Ritual Office stated: "According to the scheduled day, next year on the seventeenth day of the first month grain prayer is to be performed; two days before, a memorial announcement is to be made to the shrine of Emperor Taizu. Because that year the court will worship at the Jade Purity Hall for Wondrous Response on the fifteenth day of the first month, before Jingde 4 grain prayer used only the upper xin day; afterward it used the xin day after Beginning of Spring, since at that time there was not yet the rite of worshipping at palace temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianxi 1, the Ritual Office reported: "Under the scheduled calendar, grain prayer was set for the seventeenth day of the first month of the coming year, with a memorial announcement to Emperor Taizu's shrine two days earlier. Because the court would worship at the Jade Purity Hall for Wondrous Response on the fifteenth day of the first month, grain prayer before Jingde 4 had used only the upper xin day; afterward it used the xin day after Beginning of Spring, since worship at palace temples was not yet established.

sentences.zh: 王儉啟云：'近代明例，不以先郊後春為嫌。

translations.literal: Wang Jian submitted: 'In recent times the established precedent does not regard performing suburban sacrifice before spring as objectionable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian submitted: 'Recent established precedent does not regard suburban sacrifice before spring as objectionable.

sentences.zh: '又宋孝武朝有司奏'魏代郊天值雨，更用後辛'，或正月上辛，事有相妨，並許互用，在於禮典，固亦無嫌。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices of Emperor Xiaowu of Song also memorialized, 'In Wei, when suburban sacrifice to Heaven encountered rain, a later xin day was used.' When the upper xin day of the first month conflicts with other matters, both may be used interchangeably; in ritual canon there is likewise no objection.'"
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices under Emperor Xiaowu of Song also cited 'when rain fell on suburban Heaven sacrifice in Wei, a later xin day was used.' When the upper xin day of the first month conflicted with other rites, both dates were permitted; ritual canon raised no objection.'"

sentences.zh: 初，祈穀、大雩，皆親祀上帝。

translations.literal: At first, praying for grain and the great rain prayer were both personal sacrifices to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Initially both grain-prayer and great rain-prayer were personal sacrifices to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 由熙甯迄靖康，惟有司攝事而已。

translations.literal: From Xining through Jingkang, only the relevant offices performed by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: From Xining through Jingkang only officials performed by proxy.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，禮官言：「慶曆大雩宗祀之儀，皆用犢、羊、豕各一，唯祈穀均祀昊天上帝止用犢一。

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng, ritual officials said: "The Qingli regulations for great rain prayer and temple sacrifice all used one calf, one sheep, and one pig each; only praying for grain, when equally sacrificing to August Heaven, used only one calf.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng ritual officers noted: "Qingli great rain-prayer and temple rites each used one calf, sheep, and pig; only grain-prayer to August Heaven used a single calf.

sentences.zh: 請依雩祀、大享明堂牲牢儀，用犢、羊、豕各一。」

translations.literal: We ask to follow the rain-prayer and great Bright Hall feast victim regulations, using one calf, one sheep, and one pig each."
translations.idiomatic: They asked to match rain-prayer and Bright Hall feast practice: one calf, sheep, and pig each."

sentences.zh: 四年十月，詳定郊廟奉祀禮文所言：「近詔宗祀明堂以配上帝，其餘從祀群神悉罷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the Detailed Suburban and Temple Sacrificial Ritual Text Office said: "A recent edict temple-sacrificed at the Bright Hall with August Heaven as correlate and abolished all other attendant spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Detailed Suburban and Temple Sacrificial Ritual Text Office reported: "A recent edict paired Bright Hall temple sacrifice with August Heaven and ended all other attendant spirits.

sentences.zh: 今祈穀、大雩猶循舊制，皆群神從祀，恐與詔旨相戾。

translations.literal: Now praying for grain and the great rain prayer still follow the old system with all spirits as attendants—this may conflict with the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-prayer and great rain-prayer still follow the old system with attendant spirits—likely conflicting with the edict.

sentences.zh: 請孟春祈谷、孟夏大雩，惟祀上帝，乙太宗皇帝配，余從祀群神悉罷。」

translations.literal: We ask that in the first month of spring, praying for grain, and the first month of summer, great rain prayer, only August Heaven be sacrificed, with Emperor Taizong moved as correlate, and all other attendant spirits abolished."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that spring grain-prayer and summer great rain-prayer sacrifice only to August Heaven with Taizong as correlate, ending all other attendants."

sentences.zh: 又請改築雩壇于國南門，以嚴祀事。

translations.literal: They also asked to rebuild the rain-prayer altar at the state's south gate to enforce the sacrificial affair.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked to rebuild the rain-prayer altar at the south gate to dignify the rite.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，禮部言：「雩壇當立於圜丘之左巳地，其高一丈，廣輪四丈，周十二丈，四出陛，為三壝，各二十五步，周垣四門，一如郊壇之制。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the Ministry of Rites said: "The rain-prayer altar should stand in the si position to the left of the round mound; one zhang high, four zhang in diameter, twelve zhang in circumference, with four stairways outward, three enclosures of twenty-five paces each, and a perimeter wall with four gates—just like the suburban altar system."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year the Ministry of Rites specified: "The rain-prayer altar should stand si of the round mound: one zhang high, four zhang across, twelve zhang around, four outward stairways, three enclosures of twenty-five paces, and a walled perimeter with four gates—matching the suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年二月，禮局議以立春後上辛祈穀，詔：「以今歲孟春上辛在醜，次辛在亥，遇醜不祈而祈於亥，非禮也。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Daguan, the Ritual Bureau deliberated using the upper xin after Beginning of Spring for praying for grain; an edict said: "This year the upper xin of the first spring month is in chou and the next xin in hai—to skip chou and pray in hai is not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 4, second month, the Ritual Bureau proposed grain-prayer on the upper xin after Beginning of Spring; an edict ruled: "This year the first upper xin falls in chou and the next in hai—skipping chou for hai is uncanonical."

sentences.zh: 乃不果行。

translations.literal: So it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: So it was not held.

sentences.zh: 政和《祈穀儀》：前期降禦劄，以來年正月上辛祈穀，祀上帝。

translations.literal: Zhenghe Regulations for Praying for Grain: in the preliminary period an imperial directive was issued that in the coming year's first month, upper xin day, they would pray for grain and sacrifice to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe grain-prayer regulations: beforehand an imperial directive scheduled next year's upper xin in the first month for grain-prayer to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 前祀十日，太宰讀誓於朝堂，刑部尚書蒞之；

translations.literal: Ten days before the sacrifice, the Grand Steward read the oath in the court hall, with the Minister of Justice presiding;
translations.idiomatic: Ten days before, the Grand Steward read the oath in the court hall, with the Minister of Justice presiding;

sentences.zh: 少宰讀誓于太廟齋房，刑部侍郎蒞之。

translations.literal: the Junior Steward read the oath in the Ancestral Temple fasting chamber, with the Vice Minister of Justice presiding.
translations.idiomatic: the Junior Steward read it in the Ancestral Temple fasting chamber, with the Vice Minister of Justice presiding.

sentences.zh: 皇帝散齋七日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: The emperor observed dispersed fasting seven days and full fasting three days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fasted in seclusion seven days and in strict seclusion three days.

sentences.zh: 前祀一日，服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘玉輅，詣青城。

translations.literal: One day before the sacrifice, wearing the communication-with-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, he rode the jade chariot to the Green City.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, wearing the communication-with-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, he rode the jade chariot to the Green City.

sentences.zh: 祀日，自齋殿服通天冠、絳紗袍，乘輿至大次，服袞冕，執圭，入正門，宮架《儀安》之樂作。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, from the fasting hall in communication-with-Heaven cap and crimson gauze robe, he rode the palanquin to the great tent, donned the dragon robe and coronet, took the gui, entered the main gate, and palace-frame music "Rite's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day he left the fasting hall in cap and crimson robe, rode to the great tent, donned dragon robe and coronet, took the gui, entered the main gate, and palace-frame music "Rite's Peace" sounded.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請行事，宮架作《景安》之樂，《帝臨降康》之舞六成，止。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner requested the rite begin; palace-frame music "Scene's Peace" was performed and the dance "The Emperor Descends in Blessing" six sections, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner opened the rite; palace-frame "Scene's Peace" played and the dance "The Emperor Descends in Blessing" ran six sections, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 太常升煙，禮儀使奉請再拜。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices raised the smoke; the ritual commissioner requested a second bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices raised the smoke offering; the ritual commissioner called for a second bow.

sentences.zh: 盥洗，升壇上，登歌《嘉安》之樂作。

translations.literal: He washed hands, ascended the altar, and ascending hymn music "Fine Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: He washed, ascended the altar, and ascending hymn "Fine Peace" was performed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝搢大圭，執鎮圭，詣上帝神位前，北向，奠鎮圭於繅藉，執大圭，俯伏，興。

translations.literal: The emperor inserted the great gui, took the securing gui, proceeded before August Heaven's spirit position facing north, placed the securing gui on the silk mat, took the great gui, prostrated himself, and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor inserted the great gui, took the securing gui, approached August Heaven's spirit position facing north, placed the securing gui on the silk mat, took the great gui, prostrated, and rose.

sentences.zh: 又奏請搢大圭，跪，受玉幣。

translations.literal: They again requested that he insert the great gui, kneel, and receive the jade and silk.
