translations.idiomatic: They called for him to insert the great gui, kneel, and receive the jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 尊訖，詣太宗神位前，東向，尊幣如上儀，登歌作《仁安》之樂。

translations.literal: When the presentation was complete, he proceeded before Taizong's spirit position facing east, presented silks as in the above rite, and ascending hymn music "Benevolence's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When that was done he went before Taizong's spirit position facing east, presented silks as above, and ascending hymn "Benevolence's Peace" was performed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降階，有司進熟，禮儀使奏請執大圭，升壇，登歌《歆安》之樂作。

translations.literal: The emperor descended the steps; the relevant offices brought the cooked offerings; the ritual commissioner requested he take the great gui, ascend the altar, and ascending hymn music "Joy's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended; officials brought the cooked offerings; the ritual commissioner called for the great gui; he ascended the altar as ascending hymn "Joy's Peace" sounded.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣上帝神位前酌獻，執爵祭酒，讀冊文訖，奏請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded before August Heaven's spirit position to pour the offering, took the goblet and libated wine, finished reading the document, and they requested the emperor bow again.
translations.idiomatic: He poured the offering before August Heaven, libated with the goblet, finished reading the text, and was called to bow again.

sentences.zh: 詣太宗神位前酌獻，並如上儀，登歌作《紹安》之樂。

translations.literal: He proceeded before Taizong's spirit position to pour the offering, all as in the above rite, and ascending hymn music "Continuing Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: He did the same before Taizong, with ascending hymn "Continuing Peace."

sentences.zh: 皇帝降階，入小次，文舞退，武舞進，宮架《容安》之樂作。

translations.literal: The emperor descended the steps and entered the small tent; the civil dance withdrew and the military dance advanced; palace-frame music "Accommodation's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended into the side tent; civil dancers withdrew and military dancers advanced to palace-frame "Accommodation's Peace."

sentences.zh: 亞獻酌獻，宮架作《隆安》之樂，《神保錫羨》之舞。

translations.literal: The secondary offering poured the offering; palace-frame music "Lofty Peace" was performed and the dance "The Spirits Grant Blessings".
translations.idiomatic: The secondary offering poured the libation to palace-frame "Lofty Peace" and the dance "The Spirits Grant Blessings."

sentences.zh: 終獻如之。

translations.literal: The final offering did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The final offering did the same.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝詣飲福位，宮架《禧安》之樂作。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner requested the emperor proceed to the blessing-drinking position; palace-frame music "Felicity's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him to the blessing-drinking station as palace-frame "Felicity's Peace" played.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受爵。

translations.literal: The emperor received the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the goblet.

sentences.zh: 又請再拜。

translations.literal: They again requested a second bow.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to bow again.

sentences.zh: 有司徹俎，登歌《成安》之樂作。

translations.literal: The relevant offices removed the trays; ascending hymn music "Completion's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials cleared the trays as ascending hymn "Completion's Peace" sounded.

sentences.zh: 送神，宮架《景安》之樂作。

translations.literal: Seeing off the spirits, palace-frame music "Scene's Peace" was performed.
translations.idiomatic: As the spirits were dismissed, palace-frame "Scene's Peace" played.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣望燎位。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeded to the watching-the-burning position.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the watching-the-burning station.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，還大次。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he returned to the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended he returned to the great tent.

sentences.zh: 雩祀上帝儀亦如之。

translations.literal: The regulations for rain-prayer sacrifice to August Heaven were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Rain-prayer to August Heaven followed the same regulations.

sentences.zh: 惟太宗神位奠幣作《獻安》之樂，酌獻作《感安之樂》。

translations.literal: Only at Taizong's spirit position, presenting silks used music "Presentation's Peace," and pouring the offering used music "Gratitude's Peace."
translations.idiomatic: Only at Taizong's position did silk presentation use "Presentation's Peace" and libation "Gratitude's Peace."

sentences.zh: 南渡後，以四祀二在南郊圜壇，二在城西惠照院齋宮。

translations.literal: After the crossing south, of the four sacrifices two were at the southern-suburb round mound and two at the fasting palace of Huizhao Courtyard west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward relocation, two of the four sacrifices were held at the southern-suburb round mound and two at the Huizhao Courtyard fasting palace west of the city.

sentences.zh: 紹興十四年始具樂舞，用政和儀，增籩豆之數。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shaoxing they first provided music and dance, using Zhenghe regulations and increasing the number of offering vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 14 they first added music and dance under Zhenghe regulations, increasing offering vessels.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年，太常少卿林栗乞四祭並即圜壇，禮部侍郎鄭聞謂：「明堂當從屋祭，不當在壇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lin Li asked that all four sacrifices be held at the round mound; Vice Minister of Rites Zheng Wen said: "The Bright Hall should follow house sacrifice and not be on an altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 5, Vice Director Lin Li asked to hold all four sacrifices at the round mound; Vice Minister Zheng Wen replied: "The Bright Hall should follow house sacrifice, not an altar.

sentences.zh: 有司攝事，當於望祭殿行禮。」

translations.literal: When officials perform by proxy, the rite should be conducted at the prospect-sacrifice hall."
translations.idiomatic: When officials officiate by proxy, the rite should be at the prospect-sacrifice hall."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年，光宗受禪，始奉高宗配焉。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi, when Guangzong received the abdication, he first offered Gaozong as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 16, when Guangzong received the throne, he first paired Gaozong as correlate.

sentences.zh: 五方帝。

translations.literal: The Five-Direction Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Five-Direction Emperors.

sentences.zh: 宋因前代之制，冬至祀昊天上帝於圜丘，以五方帝、日、月、五星以下諸神從祀。

translations.literal: The Song followed former dynasties' institutions: at the winter solstice they sacrificed to August Heaven at the round mound, with the Five-Direction Emperors, sun, moon, five planets, and spirits below as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Song followed earlier practice: at the winter solstice they sacrificed to August Heaven at the round mound, with the Five-Direction Emperors, sun, moon, five planets, and lesser spirits in attendance.

sentences.zh: 又以四郊迎氣及土王日專祀五方帝，以五人帝配，五官、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: They also at the four suburbs welcomed the qi and on the Earth King day specially sacrificed to the Five-Direction Emperors, with the Five Human Emperors as correlates and the five officers, three chronograms, and seven lodges as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: They also welcomed the seasonal qi at the four suburbs and on Earth King day sacrificed specially to the Five-Direction Emperors, with the Five Human Emperors as correlates and the five officers, three chronograms, and seven lodges attending.

sentences.zh: 各建壇於國門之外：青帝之壇，其崇七尺，方六步四尺；

translations.literal: Each built an altar outside the state gate: the Green Emperor's altar seven chi high, square six paces four chi;
translations.idiomatic: Each had an altar outside the state gate: the Green Emperor's stood seven chi high, six paces four chi square;

sentences.zh: 赤帝之壇，其崇六尺，東西六步三尺，南北六步二尺；

translations.literal: the Red Emperor's altar six chi high, six paces three chi east-west and six paces two chi north-south;
translations.idiomatic: the Red Emperor's six chi high, six paces three chi by six paces two chi;

sentences.zh: 黃帝之壇，其崇四尺，方七步；

translations.literal: the Yellow Emperor's altar four chi high, square seven paces;
translations.idiomatic: the Yellow Emperor's four chi high, seven paces square;

sentences.zh: 白帝之壇，其崇七尺，方七步；

translations.literal: the White Emperor's altar seven chi high, square seven paces;
translations.idiomatic: the White Emperor's seven chi high, seven paces square;

sentences.zh: 黑帝之壇，其崇五尺，方三步七尺。

translations.literal: the Black Emperor's altar five chi high, square three paces seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: the Black Emperor's five chi high, three paces seven chi square.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，詔太常葺四郊宮，少府監遣吏齎祭服就給祠官，光祿進胙，監祭封題。

translations.literal: During Tiansheng, an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to repair the four-suburb palaces; the Palace Storehouse Commission sent clerks bearing sacrificial robes to supply the sacrifice officers; the Director of Food presented the meat portions; supervising sacrificers sealed and labeled them.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to repair the four-suburb halls; the Palace Storehouse sent clerks with robes for sacrifice officers; the Director of Food delivered portions; supervising sacrificers sealed and labeled them.

sentences.zh: 慶曆用羊、豕各一，正位大尊、著尊各二，不用犧尊，增山罍為二，壇上簠、簋、俎各增為二。

translations.literal: In Qingli they used one sheep and one pig each; for the principal position two great zun and two displayed zun, no sacrificial zun; mountain urns increased to two; on the altar grain vessels, grain tureens, and meat trays each increased to two.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qingli they used one sheep and one pig; the principal position had two great and two displayed wine vessels, no sacrificial zun; mountain urns were doubled; grain vessels and meat trays on the altar were doubled.

sentences.zh: 皇祐定壇如唐《郊祀錄》，各廣四丈，其崇用五行八七五九六為尺數。

translations.literal: In Huangyou the altars were fixed according to the Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifice, each four zhang wide; their heights used the Five Phases numbers eight, seven, five, nine, and six as chi measures.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangyou altars followed the Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifice, each four zhang wide, with heights keyed to the Five Phases numbers eight, seven, five, nine, and six.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐加羊、豕各二。

translations.literal: In Jiayou they added two sheep and two pigs each.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiayou they added two sheep and two pigs.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，知開封府範百祿言：「每歲迎氣於四郊，祀五帝，配以五神，國之大祠也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, Prefect of the Capital Fan Bailu said: "Each year welcoming the qi at the four suburbs and sacrificing to the Five Emperors, paired with the five spirits, is a great state sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 6, Capital Prefect Fan Bailu argued: "Welcoming the seasonal qi at the four suburbs each year and sacrificing to the Five Emperors with the five spirits is among the state's greatest rites.

sentences.zh: 古者天子皆親帥三公、九卿、諸侯、大夫以虔恭重事，而導四時之和氣焉。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven personally led the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, feudal lords, and grandees in reverent performance of weighty affairs, thereby guiding the harmonious qi of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven personally led the Three Dukes, Nine Ministers, lords, and grandees in reverent performance, guiding the harmonious qi of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 今吏部所差三獻皆常參官，其餘執事贊相之人皆班品卑下，不得視中祠行事者之例。

translations.literal: Now the three presentations assigned by the Ministry of Personnel are all regular-attendance officials, and the rest who conduct and assist are of low court rank—they cannot be treated by the precedent for medium sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Today the three presentations are assigned to routine court officials, and the assistants rank too low to match medium-sacrifice precedent.

sentences.zh: 請下禮部與太常議，宜以公卿攝事。」

translations.literal: We ask that the Ministry of Rites deliberate with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: dukes and ministers should perform by proxy."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices to agree that dukes and ministers should officiate."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 景德中，南郊鹵簿使王欽若言：「五方帝位板如靈威仰、赤熛怒、含樞紐、白招拒、葉光紀，恐是五帝之名，理當恭避。」

translations.literal: During Jingde, southern-suburb procession commissioner Wang Qinruo said: "The Five-Direction Emperor position boards such as Spiritual Power Gazing Aloft, Red Blazing Anger, Holding the Pivot, White Summoning Refusal, and Radiant Light Record—these may be the names of the Five Emperors and ought respectfully to be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, procession commissioner Wang Qinruo said: "The Five-Direction Emperor position boards such as Spiritual Power Gazing Aloft, Red Blazing Anger, Holding the Pivot, White Summoning Refusal, and Radiant Light Record may be the names of the Five Emperors and ought respectfully to be avoided."

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「《開寶通禮義纂》，五者皆是帝號。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "According to the Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual Compendium, all five are emperor designations.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers said: "According to the Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual Compendium, all five are imperial designations.

sentences.zh: 《漢書注》自有名，即蒼帝靈符，赤帝文祖，白帝顯紀，黑帝玄矩，黃帝神鬥是也。

translations.literal: The Book of Han commentary has its own names: Azure Emperor Spiritual Talisman, Red Emperor Literary Ancestor, White Emperor Manifest Record, Black Emperor Mysterious Square, and Yellow Emperor Spirit Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han commentary gives other names: Azure Emperor Spiritual Talisman, Red Emperor Literary Ancestor, White Emperor Manifest Record, Black Emperor Mysterious Square, and Yellow Emperor Spirit Dipper.

sentences.zh: 既為美稱，不煩回避。」

translations.literal: Since they are honorific titles, there is no need to avoid them."
translations.idiomatic: As honorific titles, avoidance was unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，以集賢校理丁諷言，按《春秋文耀勾》為五帝之名，始下太常去之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiayou, on Collation Editor Ding Feng's statement, following the Spring and Autumn Radiant Hook as the Five Emperors' names, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was first ordered to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 1, collation editor Ding Feng cited the Spring and Autumn Radiant Hook as giving the Five Emperors' names, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was ordered to remove them.

sentences.zh: 其祀儀：皇帝服袞冕，祀黑帝則服裘被袞。

translations.literal: The sacrifice regulations: the emperor wore the dragon robe and coronet; when sacrificing to the Black Emperor he wore fur over the dragon robe.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice regulations: the emperor wore dragon robe and coronet; for the Black Emperor he wore fur over the dragon robe.

sentences.zh: 配位，登歌作《承安》之樂，餘並如祈穀禮。

translations.literal: For the correlate position, ascending hymn music "Receiving Peace" was performed; the rest all followed grain-prayer regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the correlate position ascending hymn "Receiving Peace" was performed; the rest followed grain-prayer practice.

sentences.zh: 立春祀青帝，以帝太昊氏配，勾芒氏、歲星、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Spring they sacrificed to the Green Emperor, with Emperor Taihao as correlate; Goumang, the Year Star, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Beginning of Spring they sacrificed to the Green Emperor with Taihao as correlate; Goumang, the Year Star, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.

sentences.zh: 勾芒位壇下卯階之南，歲星、析木、大火、壽星位壇下子階之東，西上。

translations.literal: Goumang was south of the mao steps below the altar; the Year Star, Split Wood, Great Fire, and Longevity Star were east of the zi steps below the altar, ranked toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: Goumang stood south of the mao steps; the Year Star, Split Wood, Great Fire, and Longevity Star east of the zi steps, ranked westward.

sentences.zh: 角、亢、氐、房、心、尾、箕宿，位於壇下子階之西，東上。

translations.literal: The lodges Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket were west of the zi steps below the altar, ranked toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges Horn, Neck, Root, Room, Heart, Tail, and Winnowing Basket stood west of the zi steps, ranked eastward.

sentences.zh: 立夏祀赤帝，以帝神農氏配，祝融氏、熒惑、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Summer they sacrificed to the Red Emperor, with Emperor Shennong as correlate; Zhurong, Sparkling Deluder, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Beginning of Summer they sacrificed to the Red Emperor with Shennong as correlate; Zhurong, Sparkling Deluder, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.

sentences.zh: 祝融位壇下卯階之南，熒惑、鶉首、鶉火、鶉尾位子階之東，西上。

translations.literal: Zhurong was south of the mao steps below the altar; Sparkling Deluder, Quail Head, Quail Fire, and Quail Tail were at the zi steps, ranked toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong stood south of the mao steps; Sparkling Deluder, Quail Head, Quail Fire, and Quail Tail at the zi steps, ranked westward.

sentences.zh: 井、鬼、柳、星、張、翼、軫宿，位於壇下子階之西，東上。

translations.literal: The lodges Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot Pivot were west of the zi steps below the altar, ranked toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges Well, Ghost, Willow, Star, Extended Net, Wings, and Chariot Pivot stood west of the zi steps, ranked eastward.

sentences.zh: 季夏祀黃帝，以黃帝氏配，後土、鎮星從祀。

translations.literal: In the last month of summer they sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor, with the Yellow Emperor as correlate; Houtu and the Quiescent Star attended.
translations.idiomatic: In late summer they sacrificed to the Yellow Emperor with the Yellow Emperor as correlate; Houtu and the Quiescent Star attended.

sentences.zh: 後土位壇下卯階之南，鎮星位壇下子階之東。

translations.literal: Houtu was south of the mao steps below the altar; the Quiescent Star was east of the zi steps below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Houtu stood south of the mao steps; the Quiescent Star east of the zi steps.

sentences.zh: 立秋祀白帝，以帝少昊氏配，蓐收、太白、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Autumn they sacrificed to the White Emperor, with Emperor Shaohao as correlate; Rushou, Great White, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Beginning of Autumn they sacrificed to the White Emperor with Shaohao as correlate; Rushou, Great White, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.

sentences.zh: 蓐收位壇下卯階之南，太白、大樑、降婁、實沈位壇下子階之東，西上。

translations.literal: Rushou was south of the mao steps below the altar; Great White, Great Bridge, Descending Harvest, and Real Sink were east of the zi steps below the altar, ranked toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: Rushou stood south of the mao steps; Great White, Great Bridge, Descending Harvest, and Real Sink east of the zi steps, ranked westward.

sentences.zh: 奎、婁、胃、昴、畢、觜、參宿，位於子階之西，東上。

translations.literal: The lodges Stride, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars were west of the zi steps, ranked toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges Stride, Bond, Stomach, Hairy Head, Net, Turtle Beak, and Three Stars stood west of the zi steps, ranked eastward.

sentences.zh: 立冬祀黑帝，以帝高陽氏配，玄冥、辰星、三辰、七宿從祀。

translations.literal: At Beginning of Winter they sacrificed to the Black Emperor, with Emperor Gaoyang as correlate; Xuanming, the Chronogram Star, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.
translations.idiomatic: At Beginning of Winter they sacrificed to the Black Emperor with Gaoyang as correlate; Xuanming, the Chronogram Star, three chronograms, and seven lodges attended.

sentences.zh: 玄冥位壇下卯階之南，辰星、諏訾、玄枵、星紀位子階之東，西上。

translations.literal: Xuanming was south of the mao steps below the altar; the Chronogram Star, Zouzi, Dark Rooftree, and Star Record were at the zi steps, ranked toward the west.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming stood south of the mao steps; the Chronogram Star, Zouzi, Dark Rooftree, and Star Record at the zi steps, ranked westward.

sentences.zh: 鬥、牛、女、虛、危、室、壁宿，位子階之西，東上。

translations.literal: The lodges Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall were at the zi steps, ranked toward the east.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges Dipper, Ox, Girl, Void, Rooftop, Encampment, and Wall stood at the zi steps, ranked eastward.

sentences.zh: 紹興仍舊制，祀五帝於郊。

translations.literal: Under Shaoxing the old system remained: the Five Emperors were sacrificed to at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaoxing the old practice remained: the Five Emperors were sacrificed to at the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 感生帝，即五帝之一也。

translations.literal: The Life-Generating Emperor is one of the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Life-Generating Emperor was one of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 帝王之興，必感其一。

translations.literal: When emperors and kings rise, they must be moved by one of them.
translations.idiomatic: When emperors and kings rose, they were moved by one of them.

sentences.zh: 北齊、隋、唐皆祀之，而隋、唐以祖考升配，宋因其制。

translations.literal: Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang all sacrificed to him; Sui and Tang elevated ancestors and fathers as correlates, and Song followed their system.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi, Sui, and Tang all sacrificed to him; Sui and Tang elevated ancestors and fathers as correlates, and Song followed their system.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，太常博士聶崇義言：「皇帝以火德上承正統，請奉赤帝為感生帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite Nie Chongyi stated: "The emperor, by the virtue of fire, inherits the orthodox succession; I request that the Red Emperor be honored as the Life-Generating Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 1, Sacrifices Erudite Nie Chongyi stated: "The emperor, by the virtue of fire, inherits the orthodox succession; I request that the Red Emperor be honored as the Life-Generating Emperor.

sentences.zh: 每歲正月，別壇而祭，以符火德。」

translations.literal: Each year in the first month, sacrifice at a separate altar to accord with the virtue of fire."
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the first month, sacrifice at a separate altar to accord with the virtue of fire."

sentences.zh: 事下尚書省集議，請如崇義奏。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation, which requested approval as Chongyi had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation, which requested approval as Chongyi had memorialized.

sentences.zh: 乃酌隋制，為壇于南郊，高七尺，廣四丈，日用上辛，配以宣祖。

translations.literal: They then drew on Sui regulations, building an altar at the southern suburb seven chi high and four zhang broad, using the upper xin day, with Emperor Xuanzu as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on Sui regulations, they built an altar at the southern suburb seven chi high and four zhang broad, using the upper xin day, with Emperor Xuanzu as correlate.

sentences.zh: 牲用騂犢二，玉用四圭，有邸，幣如方色。

translations.literal: Victims were two red calves; jade was four gui with bases; silks followed the color of the direction.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were two red calves; jade was four gui with bases; silks followed the color of the direction.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，有司言：「上辛祀昊天上帝，五方帝從祀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, the responsible offices stated: "On the upper xin day August Heaven is sacrificed to, and the Five-Direction Emperors attend.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, the responsible offices stated: "On the upper xin day August Heaven is sacrificed to, and the Five-Direction Emperors attend.

sentences.zh: 今既奉赤帝為感生帝，一日之內，兩處俱祀，似為煩數。

translations.literal: Now that the Red Emperor is honored as the Life-Generating Emperor, sacrificing at two places in one day seems excessively frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Red Emperor was honored as the Life-Generating Emperor, sacrificing at two places in one day seemed excessively frequent.

sentences.zh: 況同時並祀，大禮非宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, simultaneous joint sacrifice is not proper for a great rite.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, simultaneous joint sacrifice was not proper for a great rite.

sentences.zh: 昊天從祀，請不設赤帝坐。」

translations.literal: At August Heaven's attendant sacrifice, we request that the Red Emperor's seat not be set."
translations.idiomatic: At August Heaven's attendant sacrifice, we request that the Red Emperor's seat not be set."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年九月，太常丞同判禮院謝絳言：「伏睹本院與崇文院檢討官詳定，以宣祖配感生帝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qianxing, Court of Imperial Sacrifices Aide and concurrent Ritual Academy judge Xie Jiang said: "We have seen this office and the Palace Library collation officers fix in detail that Emperor Xuanzu be correlate for the Life-Generating Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Qianxing 1, Sacrifices Aide and concurrent Ritual Academy judge Xie Jiang reported: "This office and Palace Library collation officers have fixed Emperor Xuānzǔ as correlate for the Life-Generating Emperor.

sentences.zh: 竊尋宣祖非受命開統，義或未安。

translations.literal: I privately consider that Emperor Xuanzu did not receive the Mandate and open the succession—the principle may not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzǔ did not receive the Mandate and found the succession—the pairing may not be proper.

sentences.zh: 唐武德初，圜丘、方丘、雩祀並以景帝配，祈穀、大享並以元帝配。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang Wude, round mound, square mound, and rain prayer all paired Emperor Jing; praying for grain and the great feast both paired Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang Wude, round mound, square mound, and rain prayer all paired Emperor Jing; grain-prayer and the great feast paired Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，奉高祖配圜丘、明堂、北郊，元帝配感生帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong, Gaozu was offered as correlate at round mound, Bright Hall, and northern suburb; Emperor Yuan was correlate for the Life-Generating Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizong's reign, Gaozu correlated at round mound, Bright Hall, and northern suburb; Emperor Yuan correlated for the Life-Generating Emperor.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽二年，祀高祖于圜丘，祀太宗於明堂，兼感生帝作主。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui under Gaozong, Gaozu was sacrificed to at the round mound and Taizong at the Bright Hall, with the Life-Generating Emperor also as principal.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's Yonghui 2, Gaozu was sacrificed to at the round mound and Taizong at the Bright Hall, with the Life-Generating Emperor as principal.

sentences.zh: 又以景帝、元帝稱祖，萬代不遷，停配以符古義。

translations.literal: Emperors Jing and Yuan were also styled ancestors, immovable for ten thousand generations, and their pairing was stopped to accord with ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Jing and Yuan were styled ancestors for all time, and their pairing was ended to match ancient principle.

sentences.zh: 臣以為景帝厥初受封為唐始祖，蓋與宣祖不侔。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Emperor Jing at first received enfeoffment as Tang's founding ancestor—this is not comparable to Emperor Xuanzu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing was first enfeoffed as Tang's founding ancestor—not comparable to Xuānzǔ.

sentences.zh: 宣祖于唐，是為元帝之比。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzu in Tang is comparable to Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzǔ in Tang corresponds to Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 唐有天下，裁越三世，而景、元二祖已停配典。

translations.literal: Tang held the realm for barely more than three generations, yet the pairing of ancestors Jing and Yuan was already stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tang held the realm barely three generations before Jing and Yuan pairing ended.

sentences.zh: 有宋受命，既自太祖，於今四聖，而宣祖侑祀未停，恐非往典之意。

translations.literal: The Song received the Mandate from Taizu onward; there are now four sage emperors, yet Xuānzǔ's attendant sacrifice has not stopped—this may not accord with former canon.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Mandate began with Taizu; four sage emperors have reigned, yet Xuānzǔ's attendant sacrifice continues—likely not former canon.

sentences.zh: 請依永徽故事，停宣祖配，仍用太宗故事，宗祀真宗於明堂，兼感生帝作主。

translations.literal: We ask to follow the Yonghui precedent, stop Xuānzǔ's pairing, still use Taizong's precedent of temple sacrifice to Zhenzong at the Bright Hall with the Life-Generating Emperor as principal.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to follow Yonghui precedent, end Xuānzǔ's pairing, and keep Taizong's precedent of temple sacrifice to Zhenzong at the Bright Hall with the Life-Generating Emperor as principal.

sentences.zh: 若據鄭氏說，則曰五帝迭王，王者因所感別祭，尊於南郊，以祖配之。

translations.literal: If following Master Zheng's doctrine, it says the Five Emperors rule in turn; the king sacrifices separately to the one he is moved by, honored at the southern suburb, with an ancestor as correlate.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng held that the Five Emperors rule in turn; each king sacrifices separately to the power that moved him, honored at the southern suburb with an ancestor as correlate.

sentences.zh: 今若不用武德、永徽故事，請以太祖兼配，正符鄭說。

translations.literal: If the Wude and Yonghui precedents are not used, we ask that Taizu serve as correlate—this exactly matches Master Zheng's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: If Wude and Yonghui precedents are set aside, Taizu should correlate—exactly matching Master Zheng.

sentences.zh: 詳鄭之意，非受命始封之祖不得配，故引周後稷配靈威仰之義為證。

translations.literal: Examining Master Zheng's intent, only an ancestor who received the Mandate at first enfeoffment may correlate; therefore he cites Zhou's Houji paired with Spiritual Power Gazing Aloft as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng meant only a Mandate-receiving founding ancestor may correlate, citing Zhou's Houji paired with Spiritual Power Gazing Aloft.

sentences.zh: 惟太祖始造基業，躬受符命，配侑感帝，據理甚明。

translations.literal: Only Taizu first created the foundation, personally received the talismanic command, and paired with the Life-Generating Emperor—the reasoning is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Only Taizu founded the enterprise and received the Mandate in person—pairing with the Life-Generating Emperor is clearly right.

sentences.zh: 如恐祠日相妨，當乙太宗配祈谷，太祖配雩祀，亦不失尊嚴之旨。

translations.literal: If fearing conflict of sacrifice days, Taizong may be moved to correlate for praying for grain and Taizu for rain prayer—this too does not lose the intent of dignity.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice days conflict, Taizong could correlate for grain-prayer and Taizu for rain-prayer without loss of dignity.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宣廟非惟不遷，而迭用配帝，于古為疑。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Xuānzǔ's temple should not only not be moved but also not be used in turn to pair with emperors—in antiquity this is doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzǔ's temple should not only remain unmoved but also not rotate as correlate for different emperors—doubtful by antiquity's standards.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：'祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: The Rites: 'An ancestor has merit; a temple-founder has virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: 'An ancestor has merit; a temple-founder has virtue.

sentences.zh: '但非受命之祖，親盡必毀，況配享乎？」

translations.literal: But an ancestor who did not receive the Mandate, when kinship is exhausted, must be destroyed—how much more paired sacrifice?'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet an ancestor without the Mandate, when kinship is exhausted, must be removed—how much more paired sacrifice?'"

sentences.zh: 翰林承旨李維等議：「按《禮·祭法》正義曰：'郊，謂夏正建寅之月，祭感生帝於南郊。

translations.literal: Hanlin Commissioner Li Wei and others deliberated: "According to the Correct Meaning of the Rites, Sacrifice Law: 'Suburban sacrifice means the month jianyin of summer's commencement, sacrificing to the Life-Generating Emperor at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Commissioner Li Wei and others cited the Correct Meaning of Sacrifice Law: 'Suburban sacrifice is the jianyin month, sacrificing to the Life-Generating Emperor at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: '此則崇配之文也。

translations.literal: This is the text on elevated pairing.
translations.idiomatic: This is the language of elevated pairing.

sentences.zh: 竊惟感帝比祈穀，禮秩差輕；

translations.literal: I privately consider the Life-Generating Emperor compared with praying for grain—the ritual rank is somewhat lighter;
translations.idiomatic: The Life-Generating Emperor ranks somewhat below grain-prayer;

sentences.zh: 宣祖比太祖，功業有異。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzu compared with Taizu—the achievements differ.
translations.idiomatic: Xuānzǔ's achievements differ from Taizu's.

sentences.zh: 今以太祖配祈谷，宣祖配感帝，稱情立文，於禮斯協。」

translations.literal: Now to pair Taizu with praying for grain and Xuānzǔ with the Life-Generating Emperor suits feeling and establishes text—in ritual this harmonizes.'"
translations.idiomatic: Pairing Taizu with grain-prayer and Xuānzǔ with the Life-Generating Emperor fits both feeling and ritual.'"

sentences.zh: 詔從所定。

translations.literal: An edict followed what was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict adopted their decision.

sentences.zh: 其祀儀：皇帝散齋七日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: The sacrifice regulations: the emperor observed dispersed fasting seven days and full fasting three days.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice regulations: the emperor fasted in seclusion seven days and in strict seclusion three days.

sentences.zh: 太史設帝位於壇上，北方南向，席以稿秸。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer set the emperor's position on the altar in the north facing south, with straw-mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer placed the emperor's seat on the altar's north side, facing south, on straw mats.

sentences.zh: 配帝位於壇上，東方西向，席以蒲越。

translations.literal: The correlate emperor's position was on the altar in the east facing west, with rush-mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: The correlate stood on the east side of the altar, facing west, on rush mats.

sentences.zh: 配位，奠幣，作《皇安》之樂，酌獻，作《肅安》之樂，余如祈穀祀上帝儀。

translations.literal: At the correlate position, presenting silks used music "Imperial Peace"; pouring the offering used music "Solemn Peace"; the rest followed the regulations for grain-prayer sacrifice to August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the correlate position silk presentation used "Imperial Peace" and libation "Solemn Peace"; the rest followed grain-prayer to August Heaven.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年，臣僚言：「我朝祀赤帝為感生帝，世以僖祖配之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Shaoxing, officials said: "Our dynasty sacrifices to the Red Emperor as the Life-Generating Emperor, generation after generation pairing Emperor Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 18 officials reported: "Our dynasty sacrifices to the Red Emperor as the Life-Generating Emperor, with Emperor Xīzǔ as correlate for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，奉事尤謹，故子孫眾多，與天無極。

translations.literal: Since our ancestors, service has been especially careful, so descendants are numerous and boundless as Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Since our ancestors the rite has been especially careful, so descendants are countless as Heaven.

sentences.zh: 中興浸久，祀秩咸修。

translations.literal: The restoration has grown long; sacrificial ranks are all restored.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration has matured; sacrificial ranks are largely restored.

sentences.zh: 惟感生帝，有司因循，尚淹小祀，寓於招提，酒脯而已。

translations.literal: Only the Life-Generating Emperor—the relevant offices follow routine, still treating it as a minor sacrifice housed at a roadside shrine, wine and dried meats only.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Life-Generating Emperor remains a minor rite in officials' routine, housed at a roadside shrine with wine and dried meats alone.

sentences.zh: 宜詔有司升為大祀，庶幾天意潛孚，永錫蕃衍。」

translations.literal: We should order the relevant offices to elevate it to a great sacrifice, so that Heaven's intent may be secretly aligned and perpetual increase granted."
translations.idiomatic: Officials should elevate it to a great sacrifice so Heaven's favor may endure and descendants multiply forever."

sentences.zh: 詔禮官議之，遂躋大祀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered ritual officials to deliberate, and it was promoted to a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers deliberated by edict, and it was promoted to a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禮行三獻用籩豆十二，設登歌樂舞，望祭于齋宮。

translations.literal: The rite performed three presentations with twelve offering vessels, provided ascending hymn, music, and dance, and prospect sacrifice at the fasting palace.
translations.idiomatic: The rite used three presentations and twelve offering vessels, with ascending hymn, music, and dance, and prospect sacrifice at the fasting palace.
